history.p:
When Scheibe moved to Hamburg in 1736, he became associated with the musical and intellectual environment which included composers such as Johann Mattheson and Georg Philipp Telemann. In Hamburg, Scheibe earned a living as a tutor in composition and as a keyboard player. In March 1737, he started issuing a fortnightly journal on musical subjects ranging from musical genres, styles, aesthetics, declamation, musicianship, to performance practice etc. Recounting the background in 1773, Scheibe mentions: 'I just wanted to tidy up a bit and at the same time try to improve somewhat the then prevailing bad taste in the art of composing' (SchW C1:011).
It has often been pointed out that Scheibe must have been heavily inspired by his acquaintance, Johann Christoph Gottsched’s Versuch einer kritischen Dichtkunst für die Deutschen (1730); however, it is just as likely that Scheibe found inspiration in Mattheson’s Critica musica, a journal that appeared during the years 1722–25. Later, the similarity of the titles of the two journals seems to have created some disagreement between Mattheson and Scheibe as he deals with the issue in detail in the second edition of Critischer Musikus (pp. 370–78) and briefly mentions it in a letter to Gottsched (1739). There is no doubt that also Telemann played an important role in supporting Scheibe’s idea about establishing a critical journal. They held discussions and set up a plan to publish a journal in order to 'scrutinise and expose the mistakes of the composers and all kinds of musicians in general, German as well as French' (1773; SchW C1:011). They wished also to include music examples but due to the heavy costs of setting music they decided for a lighter version. Telemann encouraged Scheibe to start on the first issues and then he would take over later on; unfortunately, Telemann did not have time so he persuaded Scheibe to continue. Apparently it had been Telemann’s intention from the start to let Scheibe carry on the project, and since the journal had already appeared in several issues, he would now have to continue and he published twenty-six sections until February 1738. However, Scheibe had so many different projects that he decided to let Der Critische Musicus rest, and first in March the following year did he continue the journal. In February 1740, he finally decided to terminate the publication.
Many of the subjects which Scheibe deals with seem to have been discussed among the musical intellectuals and occur also in the writings of Mattheson, for instance. It should be noted that Scheibe’s critique of Johann Sebastian Bach regarding his heavy compositional style was supported by Mattheson who, in his Kern melodischer Wißenschaft of 1738, characterises Bach’s fugal style in similar terms; Scheibe wrote a letter in support of Mattheson’s exposition (SchW C1:009). Furthermore, for his Grundlage einer Ehren-Pforte (1740), Mattheson had asked Bach several times to send him a biography which, however, Mattheson never received. At the same time a disagreement between Mattheson and Scheibe evolved, for in his Vollkommener Capellmeister (1739) Mattheson criticised Scheibe more or less for copying his works; Scheibe immediately responded in the June issue 1739 of Der Critische Musicus. In a letter to Gottsched in 1740, Scheibe mentions the quarrel and that there apparently was a rumour circulating the intellectual circles that he was not the author of the articles published in the journal.
Already in 1738, each article of Der Critische Musicus was extensively reviewed in Lorenz Mizlers musikalische Bibliothek; it is in particular Scheibe’s definition and exposition of the term ‘Musikus’ which receives the most extensive and critical review. Also the criticism of Bach led to several responses in Lorenz Mizlers musikalische Bibliothek. Another substantial review appeared in Beyträge zur critischen Historie (1740) apparently written by Viktoria Gottsched whom Scheibe also thanks in a letter to her husband, Johann Christoph.
During his early years as Kapellmeister in Copenhagen, Scheibe continued his correspondence with Gottsched, among others. From the letters it is apparent that since the first part of the journal was by now out of print, Scheibe was thinking about revising the entire work publishing it as one single set. In 1742, Scheibe explains his ideas concerning the revised edition to Gottsched – that is, he plans to include appendices and a completely new foreword as well as emending the errors – asking him to speak with the Breitkopf publishers in Leipzig. However, he does not have much spare time to carry out the revision due to his obligations as Kapellmeister, but he hopes to be able to send the final manuscript to Breitkopf by September 1743. It was not until 1745 that he finally managed to have a new edition published. Among the appendices which Scheibe included in the revised edition is a new translation of Aristotle’s Politics (Book VIII) made by his new acquaintance in Copenhagen, Johann Elias Schlegel, who had finished the translation already by December 1743. The new revised edition of 1745 also received an extensive and critical review by Christoph Gottlieb Schröter in Lorenz Mizlers musikalische Bibliothek.
When Scheibe died in April 1776, they started cataloguing his library with a view of holding an auction later that year. The famous Giovanni Battista Martini in Bologna heard about Scheibe's death and wrote promptly to the former Kapellmeister Paolo Scalabrini who was still working and living in Copenhagen. Martini included a list of those of Scheibe's books that he would very much like to obtain. Together with the former director of The Royal Theatre, Georg Nielsen, Scalabrini got hold of Critischer Musikus (1745) and Eine Abhandlung (1739; SchW: C1:002). He gave the the treatises to the singer Teresa Torre, who had just retired moving back to Lucca. She would then hand them over to Martini when she arrived in Italy.

annot.p: 'Ricevuta la stimat[issi]ma sua non mancai d'usa ogni diligenza per ubbidirla in ciò che riguarda le opere del fu S[igno]r Scheibe, e coll'aiuto del S[igno]r consigliere Nielsen m'è riuscito di trovare queste due che gli saranno consegnate unitam[en]te a questa mia presente dalla s[igno]ra Teresa Torre virtuosa di musica, che doppo lo spazio di otto anni che ha avuto l'onore di servire questa real corte s'è risolta di passare in Lucca sua patria.'

'Toccante le opere sue, tra poco tempo V[ostra] P[aternit]à riceverà due trattati che sono: "Il musico critico" [SchW C1:008] ed "Il trattato degl’intervalli" [SchW C1:002]. Questi li riceverà da una persona la quale presi la libertà con questa occasione di raccomandare a V[ostra] P[aternit]à. Se nella raccolta de' libri che il sud[det]to ha lasciato vi sarà qualche opera o sua o d'altri V[ostra] P[aternit]à ne sarà avvisata , non potendo per ora darle alcuna notizia, mentre si fa l'inventario adesso del tutto, e m'immagino che il tutto andrà all'incanto, p[?]vi che non mancherò d'attenzione per servirla.'
